nodes.description: Select a specialized repository workflow when an engineering request does not name a skill. Skip additional skills when ordinary coding judgment is sufficient.
Build and review tool-using agents and durable agent workflows. Use for control flow, tool contracts, memory, recovery, budgets, and delegation decisions; not ordinary AI-assisted coding.
Review API contracts for compatibility, auth, pagination, idempotency, and error semantics. Use for proposed interfaces or contract changes, rather than handler implementation.
Implement route handlers and controllers for an established API contract, including input validation, authorization, error mapping, and response serialization.
Write or review README content, API documentation, architecture notes, or operational instructions. Use when documentation is a requested deliverable or behavior changes make existing docs stale.
Review diffs, PRs, or worktrees for concrete bugs and regressions. Use adversarial review for risky production paths or when the user asks to grill a change.
Draft commit messages, PR descriptions, or release notes from verified diffs and test results. Use when delivery text is requested; do not commit or publish implicitly.
Challenge a proposed engineering approach when evidence suggests unsafe tradeoffs, speculative complexity, or conflicting constraints. Skip routine implementation with no disputed design decision.
Design or review schema changes, constraints, indexes, data lifecycle, and migration rollout. Use when durable data shape or migration behavior changes, rather than for every database query.
Search or record repository decisions with rationale, evidence, and supersession using the bundled local ledger. Use for explicit decision records or changes that revisit a prior decision.
Review abstraction quality, dependency direction, and module ownership in an architecture or refactor. Use for disputed boundaries or unnecessary complexity, rather than routine edits.
Create a fill-in Markdown PRD, project brief, RFC, or engineering design template from the bundled assets. Use when the user wants a template, rather than a completed strategy.

Develop frontend design directions from Dribbble references, screenshots, or existing UI. Use for visual inspiration, moodboards, hierarchy, typography, and design critiques; not mechanical frontend fixes.
Design and review knowledge graphs, dependency graphs, and GraphRAG pipelines. Use for entity identity, provenance, temporal facts, traversal, or graph retrieval quality; not workflow orchestration.
Design and improve coding-agent environments, feedback loops, and evaluation harnesses. Use for reproducibility, task verification, context handoffs, or measured agent reliability.
Plan changes with meaningful sequencing, migration, rollout, or validation dependencies. Use when a plan is requested or execution needs coordination; skip formal plans for straightforward edits.
Triage production degradation and assess mitigation, rollback, or hotfix options. Use during an active incident or when preparing its post-mortem.
Schedule local macOS notifications with the bundled launchd script. Use for reminder requests with a message and due time; clarify missing or ambiguous timing.
Design or audit service logs, metrics, traces, SLOs, dashboards, and alerts. Use for instrumentation changes, telemetry gaps, logging noise, or actionable paging.

Draft stakeholder or customer messages that communicate disagreement, tradeoffs, status, or decisions respectfully and firmly. Use for substantive product communication, rather than every short reply.
Evaluate startup product bets, MVP scope, onboarding, pricing, or competitor-driven requests. Use when user value, differentiation, or learning needs a decision, rather than every UI edit.
Generate or refresh a repository file and symbol map using bundled scripts. Use for broad discovery in an unfamiliar or large repository; skip mapping when the relevant files are already known.
Review changed trust boundaries for reachable security and privacy failures: auth, tenant isolation, secrets, uploads, webhooks, injection, and dependency trust.
Maintain skills, triggers, routing, and supporting validation when requested or when usage reveals a concrete failure. Use for evidence-backed skill changes, rather than unrelated feature work.
Implement business workflows with transaction, permission, retry, and external side-effect boundaries. Use for application orchestration that needs explicit failure handling.
Review test adequacy, false confidence, mocks, flakiness, and missing risk coverage. Use when test strategy is uncertain or a test review is requested, rather than every test edit.
Curate verified learning resources and a practical learning path. Use when the user asks to study a domain, upskill, or find current technical reading and talks.
Record evidence-backed accomplishments or generate appraisal summaries using the bundled private local worklog. Use for brag documents, work-impact capture, and performance reviews.

Reset work when there is observable thrash, repeated failure without new evidence, scope drift, or a contradiction with the active goal. Use for a concrete course correction, rather than routine uncertainty.
